## Load packages

```{r setup}
pacman::p_load(here, limpa, limma, dplyr, ggplot2, purrr, tibble, tidyr, writexl)
here::i_am("02_Differential_Expression/02_Differential/a_script/02_differential.qmd")
```

## Read proteins and design

`proteins` holds the normalised log2 abundances and their standard errors; `d` holds the design,
the contrasts and the baseline contrast's name. Design rows and matrix columns must name the same
samples in the same order; equal dimensions alone would not catch a swapped sample.

```{r read}
proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
d <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "01_Design", "c_data", "design.rds"))
fitted_slope_file <- here(
  "01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "quant_runs", "proteins_slope_fitted.rds"
)

stopifnot(identical(rownames(d$design), colnames(proteins$E)))
```

## Fit

limpa's sequence is `dpcDE()`, `contrasts.fit()`, `eBayes()`, `topTable()`. `dpcDE()` takes the
place of `lmFit()` because only it reads the standard errors from `dpcQuant()`, as precision
weights. `sample.weights = TRUE` adds one quality weight per sample, since removing contaminant
rows does not undo what a bloody biopsy did to the rest of the sample; the weights are saved before
`contrasts.fit()`, which drops them. `contrasts.fit()` forms the five comparisons and `eBayes()`
moderates each protein's variance toward a prior fitted across all proteins; `robust = TRUE` keeps
proteins with outlying variances from distorting that prior.

```{r fit}
fit <- dpcDE(proteins, d$design, sample.weights = TRUE)
sample_weights <- fit$targets$sample.weight
fit <- contrasts.fit(fit, d$contrasts)
fit <- eBayes(fit, robust = TRUE)
```

A lower weight reduces a sample's contribution without dropping it. Weights that differ between
groups deserve a look but do not by themselves invalidate the model.

```{r sample-weights}
tibble(group = proteins$targets$group, weight = sample_weights) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(), median_weight = round(median(weight), 2),
    lowest_weight = round(min(weight), 2), .by = group
  )
```

From the fitted standard errors, the interaction effect each protein would need for 80% power at
an unadjusted two-sided 0.05 threshold, on the log2 scale: median and 90th percentile across
proteins. It describes sensitivity; it is not an FDR-adjusted power analysis or evidence of
equivalence.

```{r detectable-effect}
se <- fit$stdev.unscaled[, "Modality_x_Time_Interaction"] * sqrt(fit$s2.post)
round(quantile(se * (qt(0.975, fit$df.total) + qt(0.80, fit$df.total)), c(0.5, 0.9)), 3)
```

## Results

`topTable()` takes the fit and one contrast and returns one row per protein. `sort.by = "none"`
keeps protein order (the default sorts on the B statistic). Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) adjustment
controls the false discovery rate within each contrast, not across all five.

```{r results}
results <- map(colnames(d$contrasts), function(cn) {
  topTable(fit, coef = cn, number = Inf, sort.by = "none") |>
    rownames_to_column("protein") |>
    mutate(contrast = cn, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

contrast_summary <- results |>
  summarise(
    n_tested = n(),
    n_fdr_05 = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.05),
    n_fdr_10 = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.10),
    min_adj_p = min(adj.P.Val),
    .by = contrast
  )
contrast_summary |>
  mutate(min_adj_p = signif(min_adj_p, 3))
```

## Inspect p-value distributions

Per contrast: the estimated share of true nulls (`propTrueNull()`), the median absolute t and the
fraction of p below 0.2. They describe the distributions; they do not prove calibration or explain
an absence of discoveries.

```{r null-calibration}
null_summary <- results |>
  summarise(
    prop_true_null = round(propTrueNull(P.Value), 3),
    median_abs_t = round(median(abs(t)), 3),
    p_below_0.2 = round(mean(P.Value < 0.2), 3), .by = contrast
  )
null_summary
```

The dashed line is the count per bin if p-values were uniform.

```{r p-histogram}
ggplot(results, aes(P.Value)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0, fill = "grey35") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = nrow(proteins) / 20, linetype = 2, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~contrast) +
  labs(x = "p", y = "proteins", caption = "dashed line marks a flat null") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Significant and large enough

`treat()` tests whether |logFC| exceeds a threshold, here `log2(1.15)`, a 15% change, rather than
filtering significant results on fold change afterwards, which controls no error rate. The
threshold is a study choice fixed in advance, not swept; its rationale is not yet documented.

```{r treat}
ft <- treat(fit, lfc = log2(1.15), robust = TRUE)
treat_summary <- enframe(colSums(decideTests(ft) != 0), "contrast", "n_q_05")
treat_summary
```

## The pi score

The pi score, `P.Value^abs(logFC)`, ranks the two within-leg contrasts so that large effects with
small p come first. It controls no error rate and selects nothing. The mean number of observed
precursors per sample sits beside it, because the top of a pi ranking is often thinly observed.

```{r pi-ranking}
obs_per_sample <- rowMeans(proteins$other$n.observations)

results |>
  filter(contrast %in% c("BFR_Post-Pre", "HLRT_Post-Pre")) |>
  mutate(pi_score = P.Value^abs(logFC)) |>
  slice_min(pi_score, n = 10, by = contrast) |>
  mutate(mean_obs = round(obs_per_sample[protein], 2)) |>
  select(contrast, protein, Genes, logFC, adj.P.Val, pi_score, NPrec, mean_obs)
```

## Baseline comparison

The two legs before training. A difference here can be biological or technical; it is not
automatically an upstream error. The row check guards against a contrast name that matches nothing,
since `sum(logical(0))` is zero and would look like an empty baseline.

```{r baseline}
baseline <- filter(results, contrast == d$baseline)
stopifnot(nrow(baseline) == nrow(proteins))
sum(baseline$adj.P.Val < 0.05)

slice_min(baseline, P.Value, n = 5) |>
  select(protein, Genes, logFC, P.Value, adj.P.Val)
```

The count is printed, not asserted, so a difference lands in the report instead of halting it.

## Slope sensitivity

When the fitted-slope checkpoint exists, it gets the same detection filter, normalisation and
design, then the discovery counts are compared with the primary run. The checks confirm sample
order and protein coverage; they cannot confirm the checkpoint came from the same precursors.

```{r slope-sensitivity}
#| eval: !expr file.exists(fitted_slope_file)
fitted_slope <- readRDS(fitted_slope_file)
fitted_slope <- fitted_slope[
  filterByDetection(fitted_slope, n.samples = min(table(fitted_slope$targets$group))),
]
fitted_slope$E <- normalizeBetweenArrays(fitted_slope$E, method = "cyclicloess")
stopifnot(identical(colnames(fitted_slope$E), rownames(d$design)))
refit <- dpcDE(fitted_slope, d$design, sample.weights = TRUE) |>
  contrasts.fit(d$contrasts) |>
  eBayes(robust = TRUE)
primary_hits <- decideTests(fit) != 0
stopifnot(all(rownames(primary_hits) %in% rownames(refit)))
refit_hits <- decideTests(refit)[rownames(primary_hits), , drop = FALSE] != 0
rbind(
  slope_0.7 = colSums(primary_hits),
  fitted_curve = colSums(refit_hits),
  both = colSums(primary_hits & refit_hits)
)
```

## Save results

`fit.rds` keeps the fitted model for the stages that rebuild contrasts. `02_differential.xlsx`
holds `DEP_matrix` (one row per protein: log2 fold change, p and BH-adjusted p per contrast),
discovery counts, sample weights and the distribution summaries.

```{r write}
dep_matrix <- results |>
  select(protein, Genes, NPrec, contrast, logFC, P.Value, adj.P.Val) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = contrast,
    values_from = c(logFC, P.Value, adj.P.Val),
    names_glue = "{contrast}_{.value}"
  )

out <- here("02_Differential_Expression", "02_Differential", "c_data")
saveRDS(fit, file.path(out, "fit.rds"))
sheets <- list(
  DEP_matrix = dep_matrix,
  contrast_summary = contrast_summary,
  sample_weights = data.frame(
    sample_id = colnames(proteins$E), group = proteins$targets$group, weight = sample_weights
  ),
  null_summary = null_summary,
  treat_summary = treat_summary
)
overview <- data.frame(
  sheet = names(sheets), rows = map_int(sheets, nrow), columns = map_int(sheets, ncol),
  description = c(
    "logFC, p and BH p per contrast",
    "Discoveries per contrast at FDR 0.05 and 0.10",
    "Sample identifiers, groups and quality weights",
    "Descriptive p-value and t-statistic summaries",
    "Discoveries against the 15 percent fold-change threshold"
  )
)
write_xlsx(c(list(overview = overview), sheets), file.path(out, "02_differential.xlsx"))
```
